- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 85+ → 86+), then sharply correct downward.
- Mean reversion is strong in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window; model fails to reflect this, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — underestimates when prices fall sharply from prior days.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, especially when historical mean is above 80 — model fails to account for downward momentum.
- When true price drops below 75, model often fails to adjust downward, continuing to predict 78–82 range.
- Model underestimates when true price is near 70–75, especially if preceded by a spike — fails to recognize “recovery” or “rebound” phase.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values when historical 30-day average is above 80 — model overweights recent highs.
- Model does not adjust for seasonal or calendar-based patterns (e.g., end-of-month dips, weekly volatility) — assumes linear trend.
- When true price is below 70, model often predicts 70–75, missing the sharp drop or plateau — underestimates volatility in low-price regimes.
